1) aligning image and word representations improves inductive transfer across vision-language tasks, 2) this is achieved by forcing the two tasks to use the same embeddings, and 3) the benefit is especially large for recognition of categories that have few labels but are common in the VQA task.

1) aligning visual recognition and visual question answering by using the same word-region representations leads to better inductive transfer than standard multitasking learning, and 2) this alignment improves visual recognition, especially for categories with few training labels but many VQA examples.
